# WebSpectrometer2.0

> Free, open-source software for DIY and webcam spectrometers that runs entirely in the browser. It converts the spectral image captured by a webcam spectrometer (or a TCD1304/TCD1254 linear CCD sensor over Web Serial) into a live, calibrated spectrum and computes light-quality, UV, transmission and absorbance results.

## What it is

WebSpectrometer2.0 is a standalone continuation of jayden-sudo/WebSpectrometer (a browser port of the Windows program Theremino Spectrometer V5.0). It runs in any Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave…) on Linux, macOS and Windows; Firefox and Safari are not supported (no Web Serial). All image processing happens locally in the browser; no video or spectrum data is uploaded. License: GNU GPL v3.

## Key capabilities

- Live spectrum from a UVC webcam spectrometer (e.g. Little Garden Spectrometer) or a TCD1304/TCD1254 linear sensor.
- Wavelength calibration: manual multi-point (Trim points) or automatic from reference lamps (fluorescent/CFL, UVC Hg/Ar, neon, sodium, hydrogen, helium, sunlight Fraunhofer lines).
- Spectral response calibration: incandescent / halogen presets (Planck curve), CIE illuminant A, custom colour temperature, or a tabulated reference spectrum file (e.g. a ground-level solar spectrum, with O2/H2O absorption bands skipped).
- Light quality: CCT, Duv, x/y, CRI Ra and R1–R14 (R9), luminous efficacy of radiation, illuminance; CCT/CRI only for white light (|Duv| ≤ 0.05).
- UV: UV-A share (340–400 nm), UVC/UVB/UVA/visible/IR band bar under the graph.
- Spectral line identification (Hg, Ar, Ne, Na, H, He, CFL phosphors, Fraunhofer); 2nd- and 3rd-order diffraction ghosts flagged instead of misidentified.
- FWHM, spectrum comparison per band, HDR, time log, saturation warning.
- Transmission of glasses, filters and windows (τv, sunglass category, UV/HEV/IR blocking); absorbance with Beer–Lambert.
- CSV/TXT export compatible with Theremino Spectrometer files, image export, HTML/PDF report.
- Interface: English and Polish (base features also in Chinese, Italian, French, Portuguese).

## How to use (typical flow)

1. Open the site in Chrome or Edge (camera requires HTTPS), connect the spectrometer camera, set manual exposure.
2. Calibrate wavelengths with a fluorescent or UVC lamp (Tools → Auto calibration…).
3. Calibrate the spectral response with an incandescent or halogen lamp (Light quality → Calibration & details…), then enable "Corrected".
4. Measure light sources; use a diffuser on the slit, avoid saturation.
